abstract: BACKGROUND: Ovarian Mature Cystic Teratomas (MCTs), the most common type of ovarian teratoma, contain tissues from all three germ layers. The "floating ball sign," which consists of mobile spherules of sebum and keratin, is a characteristic feature seen on Computed Tomography (CT) and Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI). However, the imaging features can overlap with other cystic lesions, leading to potential misdiagnosis. This case report focuses on a giant MCT initially misdiagnosed as hydatid disease on CT. Its value lies in highlighting the diagnostic pitfall of over-relying on CT and demonstrating how a systematic, multimodal approach resolves uncertainty. CASE PRESENTATION: A 40-year-old female presented to our hospital due to a 3-month history of progressive, painless abdominal distension and recent urinary frequency/urgency. On physical examination, a soft, non-tender mass was palpated in the umbilical region. Initial abdominal-pelvic contrastenhanced CT revealed a huge cystic lesion with multiple internal cystic structures resembling "daughter cysts", a feature suggestive of hydatid disease. However, preoperative parasite tests returned negative, creating a conflict with this initial suspicion, and the mass effect caused by the lesion obscured its origin on CT. This discrepancy prompted further evaluation, which revealed mobile intracystic spherical structures via targeted ultrasound, confirming their mobility and floatability. Meanwhile, MRI identified characteristic fat content through fat-saturated sequences. These findings confirm the "floating ball sign," which collectively supported the possible diagnosis of MCT. The diagnosis was confirmed by exploratory laparotomy and subsequent histopathological analysis. CONCLUSION: This case illustrates that while CT is useful for initial evaluation of giant abdominopelvic masses, its findings can be misleading. When imaging and clinical data conflict, a deliberate diagnostic reconsideration pathway using targeted ultrasound and MRI is key to avoiding misdiagnosis.
abstract_ja: 背景：卵巣成熟嚢胞性奇形腫は最も多い卵巣奇形腫であり、三胚葉すべての組織を含む。「浮遊球徴候」は、皮脂と角化物からなる可動性の球体で、コンピュータ断層撮影(CT)と磁気共鳴画像法(MRI)で見られる特徴的所見である。しかし、画像所見は他の嚢胞性病変と重なりうるため、誤診につながる可能性がある。本症例報告は、CTで包虫症と誤診された巨大な成熟嚢胞性奇形腫に焦点を当てる。その価値は、CTに過度に依存することの診断上の落とし穴を示し、系統的なマルチモダリティ・アプローチが不確実性をどのように解決するかを示す点にある。症例提示：40歳女性が3か月間の進行性で無痛性の腹部膨満と、最近の頻尿・尿意切迫を訴えて受診した。身体診察で臍部に柔らかく非圧痛性の腫瘤を触知した。初回の造影腹骨盤部CTで、包虫症を示唆する「娘嚢胞」様の多数の内部嚢胞構造を伴う巨大な嚢胞性病変を認めた。しかし術前の寄生虫検査は陰性で、初回の疑いと矛盾した。腫瘤効果により病変の起源はCTでは不明瞭であった。そこで追加評価を行い、標的を絞った超音波検査で可動性のある嚢胞内球状構造が確認され、その可動性と浮遊性が確かめられた。一方、脂肪抑制シーケンスのMRIで特徴的な脂肪成分が同定された。これらの所見は「浮遊球徴候」を確認し、成熟嚢胞性奇形腫の可能性を支持した。診断は開腹手術と病理組織学的解析により確定した。結論：CTは巨大な腹骨盤部腫瘤の初期評価に有用であるが、その所見は誤解を招く場合がある。画像所見と臨床データが矛盾する場合、標的超音波検査とMRIを用いた意図的な診断の再検討が、誤診を避けるための鍵となる。
